titleStmt.title: Physical Layer Security in Multicarrier OFDM Systems using Convex Optimization

publicationStmt.publisher: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications

analytic.title: Physical Layer Security in Multicarrier OFDM Systems using Convex Optimization

abstract.p: In this paper, we propose Secure Optimal Subcarrier Power Allocation (SOSPA) for multicarrier OFDM transmissions. To protect communications against eavesdropping, we apply Physical Layer Security principles rooted in Information Theory. The transmitter employs Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) to synthesize orthogonal subcarriers. We formulate secrecy rate maximization as a Convex Optimization problem solved via Gradient Descent.

div.head: 1. Introduction
div.p: Information Theory establishes the fundamental limits of secure wireless communications through Physical Layer Security [1]. In multicarrier communications, OFDM provides high spectral efficiency and robustness against multipath fading.

div.head: 2. Signal Model and Frequency Transform
div.p: The continuous Fourier Transform underlies discrete multicarrier representations. At the transmitter, the IFFT algorithm modulates frequency domain data symbols into time-domain orthogonal waveforms:

formula.latex: x[n] = \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} X[k] e^{j 2 \pi k n / N}

div.p: At the receiver, the FFT algorithm recovers the original symbols from the received signal.

div.head: 3. Power Allocation via Convex Optimization
div.p: The secrecy rate allocation over N subcarriers is formulated as a Convex Optimization problem subject to total power budget P_total:
Because the objective function is concave over feasible subcarrier channels, iterative Gradient Descent converges monotonically to the global optimum [2].

div.head: 4. Proposed Methodology: Secure Optimal Subcarrier Power Allocation
div.p: We propose Secure Optimal Subcarrier Power Allocation (SOSPA). Subcarriers where legitimate channel gain exceeds eavesdropper channel gain are allocated transmit power according to water-filling principles derived from convex optimization.
